d: Some careers shine brighter than others
If you’re looking for a career that will help you stand out, join HSBC and fulfil your potential.

HSBC Corporate and Institutional Banking (CIB) is a markets-led, financing-focused business that provides investment and financial solutions. Through our international network, we connect emerging and mature markets, covering key growth areas. We partner with our corporate, government and institutional clients to help them achieve consistent, long-term performance. Our products and services include advisory, financing, prime services, research and analysis, securities services, trading and sales and transaction banking.

HSBC Global Research is an independent research house with a strong focus on Emerging Markets (EMs). We have 300 analysts covering 1,600+ companies, 60+ economies, 45+ sovereigns’ rates and 50+ currencies globally. Our analysts, based out of 20 countries, are spread across Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Americas, the Middle East and Africa. Our goal is to generate unique investment opportunities for our clients by sharing our insights and creating thought-provoking ideas

We are seeking an ambitious individual to join HSBC Global Research in Dubai as an Equity Analyst. In addition to achieving own scorecard metrics, the individual will be required to work together with colleagues to manage and achieve divisional business targets.
q: Some experience in equity research, investment analysis, investment banking, asset management or a related financial services discipline

Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present clear, well-supported investment views to professional audiences
Strong research, attention to detail and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
A collaborative and intellectually curious approach, with the confidence to work independently and engage effectively with senior colleagues, clients and company management teams.

A full-time graduation degree of at least three years is essential for obtaining a UAE visa and/or work permit. For degrees obtained outside the UAE, valid attestations and equivalency are also mandatory.

The Compliance Operations Specialist supports the day-to-day execution of Bybit's global compliance operations programme.

Working across multiple licensed jurisdictions, you will help ensure regulatory commitments are translated into practical operating processes, tracked effectively, and maintained throughout the licence lifecycle. This role works closely with Legal, Licensing, Product, Operations and regional teams to support operational readiness and ongoing compliance activities.
q: 2 - 4 years experience in Compliance Operations, Regulatory Operations, Project Management Office or a similar operational role within financial services, fintech or another regulated industry.
Experience coordinating cross-functional projects or operational initiatives, working with stakeholders across different functions and jurisdictions
Strong organisational and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams, follow through on deliverables and work independently with minimal supervision.
Ability to develop clear SOPs, process documentation and management reports.
Comfortable working independently in a fast-paced environment with competing priorities.
Crypto or digital asset experience is advantageous but not essential.
Fluency in English (written and spoken) is required.
Mandarin proficiency is advantageous to support collaboration with Mandarin-speaking stakeholders.
Passionate about cryptocurrency and financial innovation.
Highly organised with strong follow-through and execution discipline.
Collaborative and comfortable working with legal, product, operations and business stakeholders.
Comfortable using AI tools to improve productivity, documentation quality and operational efficiency.
r: Manage the tracking of regulatory obligations, licensing conditions and operational actions, coordinating with stakeholders to ensure timely completion.
Coordinate the operational implementation of new licences, including developing SOPs, implementation checklists and business readiness materials in collaboration with relevant stakeholders
Monitor adherence to compliance operational processes, proactively identifying, managing and escalating risks or overdue actions.
Prepare operational reports, implementation updates and management briefing materials for senior stakeholders.
Coordinate cross-functional regulatory implementation activities with Legal, Licensing, Product, Operations and regional teams.
Support audits, regulatory inspections and operational reviews by coordinating documentation, evidence gathering and remediation tracking.
Conduct operational gap assessments, identify areas for improvement and drive remediation initiatives to strengthen compliance processes and controls.

d: DP World Jeddah is looking for an experienced Advanced Yard Planner to join our Planning team.

The Advanced Yard Planner develops forward-looking yard plans, capacity forecasts and optimization recommendations to align yard strategy with vessel schedules, gate demand, inventory and equipment capability. The role improves planning parameters and allocation strategies, anticipates congestion, reduces re-handles and supports data-driven continuous improvement across terminal operations.
q: Education: Bachelor’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain, Maritime Studies, Engineering, Industrial Engineering or a related field.
Experience: 4+ years in container terminal operations, including substantial experience in yard planning, terminal planning or operational optimization.

TOS and planning systems: Strong practical knowledge of a TOS, preferably Zodiac, EasyTOS or a comparable system, including allocation rules, planning parameters, filters and automated planning workflows.
Yard strategy: Strong understanding of yard layout, block profiles, capacity management, stacking strategies, equipment constraints and cargo segregation, including reefer, OOG and IMDG requirements.
Forecasting and analysis: Ability to analyze vessel volumes, inventory, dwell time, gate forecasts, utilization and re-handle data to forecast capacity and identify operational risks.
Optimization and problem-solving: Able to investigate root causes, develop scenarios, evaluate trade-offs and recommend changes that improve space utilization and reduce unproductive moves.
Systems and reporting: Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookup functions, charts and structured reporting; experience with dashboards or data-analysis tools is an advantage.
Project and stakeholder coordination: Able to work with Yard Strategists, Vessel Planners, Operations, IT/TOS and management on system testing, parameter changes and improvement initiatives.
Communication and ownership: Strong written and verbal English, analytical thinking, attention to detail, sound judgment and accountability; Arabic is an advantage.
Work environment: Willing to work shifts or general hours, including weekends and public holidays when required, in accordance with company policy and applicable labor laws.
r: Prepare forward-looking yard plans for vessels expected within the next 24–72 hours and maintain a rolling view of upcoming vessel volumes, gate demand, inventory and available capacity.
Develop allocation strategies for import, export, transshipment, empty, reefer, IMDG, OOG and special cargo, ensuring compliance with approved yard strategy, segregation requirements and SOPs.

Forecast yard utilization, block occupancy, stacking density and capacity pressure by block and time period; identify risks early and propose mitigation plans before capacity constraints affect operations.
Coordinate with Vessel Planners to align yard plans with vessel schedules, stowage and loading sequences, POD, container size, weight class and cargo-specific requirements.
Design and refine allocation approaches across RTG/AeRTG/ECH and other applicable blocks, balancing capacity, equipment capability, workload, accessibility and expected cargo flows.
Analyze re-handle ratios, housekeeping moves, mixed stacks, dwell time, gate demand and yard-related vessel delays to identify root causes and develop measurable improvement actions.
Review yard planning filters, groups, ranges, stacking rules and TOS parameters; work with the Yard Strategist and IT/TOS teams to test and improve automated and manual planning processes.
Develop planning scenarios for peak volumes, high yard utilization, empty-container surges, equipment constraints and changes to vessel schedules; recommend practical contingency plans.
Establish and maintain planning reports, forecasts and dashboards to support decisions on yard capacity, cargo allocation, reefer plug requirements and operational performance.
Review long-staying containers, overstays and empty inventory trends with relevant teams and shipping lines; assess their impact on future capacity and recommend actions.
Define and communicate yard planning standards, allocation principles and handover requirements; support knowledge sharing and consistent planning practices across shifts.
Support TOS upgrades, user acceptance testing, planning-system enhancements and continuous improvement projects; document requirements, test outcomes and recommended changes.
Provide the supervisor and management with clear analysis of capacity risks, plan deviations, root causes, proposed actions and expected operational benefits.
If you have experience in yard planning and container terminal operations, and are ready to contribute to operational excellence, we encourage you to apply.
